title: Quantum state preparation for weighted d-DNNF
authors: Steef Hegeman, Joon Hyung Lee, Alfons Laarman
abstract: The quantum state preparation problem is to, given a description of a quantum state, efficiently generate a quantum circuit computing the state. We show that for quantum states described by weighted d-DNNF (deterministic, decomposable pseudo-Boolean circuits) a quantum circuit computing the state can be obtained in linear time up to complex arithmetic.
summary: This paper solves the Quantum State Preparation Problem for states defined by weighted d-DNNF circuits. It constructs an efficient quantum circuit $Q(D)$ using three distinct layers—certificate propagation, nonzero computation, and reset—to prepare the target state. The resulting circuit exhibits polynomial complexity bounds in terms of the size and depth of the input d-DNNF.
main_problem: The paper addresses the Quantum State Preparation Problem (QSP): efficiently generating a quantum circuit that prepares a target quantum state given its description.
main_result: It provides explicit constructions showing that for states described by weighted d-DNNF, the required quantum circuit can be generated with polynomial complexity in the size of the description.
method: The construction involves designing a quantum circuit $Q(D)$ structured in three layers—certificate propagation, nonzero computation, and reset—utilizing gates from $\{X, CX\} \cup SU(2)$.
model_or_system: The quantum state is defined by the weighted d-DNNF (deterministic, decomposable pseudo-Boolean circuit) $D$. The target state is typically $S_2(D) = \sum_{x} D(x) |xangle$.
key_observables: Circuit complexity metrics: Size ($|D|$), Depth ($	ext{depth}(D)$), and Width.
important_parameters: The complexity bounds are $O(|D|)$ gates, $O(	ext{depth}(D))$ depth (for 2-d-DNNF), and $O(|D|)$ width.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a computational RAM model where complex arithmetic operations are constant time. It also relies on the structure of certificates within the d-DNNF.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates a weighted 2-d-DNNF example. Figure 2 shows a normalized weighted 2-d-DNNF. Figure 3 displays the resulting quantum circuit $Q(D)$ composed of the three distinct functional layers.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem and then details the construction of the circuit $Q(D)$ in three sequential layers: certificate propagation, nonzero layer, and reset layer. It proves correctness and analyzes the resulting complexity bounds.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, efficient quantum circuit constructions for preparing states defined by classical computational structures (d-DNNF), which is fundamental knowledge for designing quantum algorithms and simulating quantum processes.
